concept.name: Clean price
concept.definition: The standard quoted market price of a bond, stated net of accrued interest — the price shown on screens and used for price comparison, as distinct from the full amount actually paid at settlement.
concept.intuition: The clean price strips out the mechanical day-count drift so price changes reflect real market moves, not just time passing between coupon dates.
concept.mechanics: By market convention bonds are quoted clean; the amount the buyer actually pays is the dirty price = clean price + accrued interest. Quoting clean prevents the sawtooth pattern the dirty price would otherwise show as interest accrues and then drops at each coupon payment.
concept.formula: Clean price = dirty price - accrued interest.
concept.failure_modes: Computing realized return or cash needs from the clean price alone understates the settlement cash outlay by the accrued interest; comparing yields from dirty cash flows against clean quotes without adjustment creates small pricing inconsistencies.
concept.misconceptions: The clean price is not the price you pay: settlement always uses the dirty (full) price, so cash planning based on quoted prices alone will be short by the accrued amount.
concept.example: A bond quoted at 98.50 (clean) with $7.50 accrued interest per $100 face requires a payment of $106.00 per $100 face — the dirty price — at settlement.

citations.source: Hillier et al., Fundamentals of Corporate Finance, Chapter 6: Bond Valuation (McGraw-Hill sample chapter)
citations.section: A Note about Bond Price Quotes
